frosted blueberry banana loaf ð« 

im super picky about banana bread and my husband loves when i make it, so i love spicing it up in different ways! this bread is loaded with blueberries and so yummy! hereâs how i made it :) 

ingredients:
3 very ripe bananas 
3/4 cup maple syrup 
1/3 cup oil (i like avocado oil) 
1 tsp vanilla 
1 egg
1 tsp baking soda 
1 tsp baking powder 
1/4 tsp salt 
1 1/2 cups AP flour 
2 cups wild blueberries 

make it:
in a bowl, mash bananas until you can mix well. next add wet ingredients: maple syrup, oil, eggs, and vanilla. once wet ingredients are mixed in, add baking soda, baking powder and salt. slowly add in flour, careful not to over mix. add in blueberries. pour into a bread pan and top with more blueberries if youâd like. 

bake at 350 for about an hour and 10 minutes to an hour and 30 minutes. baking time will vary depending on if you use fresh or frozen blueberries. i love frozen wild blueberries but the baking time is more like an hour and 30 because of the extra moisture, so just be aware! the bread is done when a toothpick comes out clean or mostly clean :) 

for the glaze, i added 2 cups of powdered sugar into a bowl along with a tsp of vanilla and a handful of mashed blueberries. mix while slowly adding a couple splashes of heavy cream until you get a super thick and creamy consistency. pour ontop of cooled bread and let set for about 10 minutes and serve! if youâd love blueberries like me i hope you love this :)

Two-Block Haircut and fade( Curtain Style)

Overview

âTwo-Block haircut features a distinct contrast between two main sections: the sides and back are trimmed short (often undercut or tapered), while the top and crown are left long and textured. In this specific image, it is styled with a middle-part curtain (or "comma hair" shape), giving it a voluminous, effortlessly wavy, and modern look.

âHow to Style

âPrep: Start with damp hair. Apply a lightweight volume mousse or a heat protectant.

âBlow-dry: Use a roller brush or your fingers while blow-drying. Dry the roots upward to create volume at the crown, and blow-dry the front fringe away from your face to create that signature "C" or curtain curve.

âFinish: Rub a small amount of lightweight wax, pomade, or texture powder into your hands and run it through the top to define the texture.

âLock: Use a light-hold hairspray to keep the curtain shape in place without making the hair stiff.

âMaintenance

âTrimming: To keep the contrast sharp, youâll need a trim every 3 to 4 weeks for the sides and back. The top can grow a bit longer depending on your preference.

âHair Care: Since this style relies on volume and texture, use a volumizing shampoo and avoid heavy conditioners that can weigh the hair down.

Cook time: 15 minutes Serves: 2

Â¼ cup corn starch
1 tsp paprika
Â½ tsp garlic powder
Â½ tsp salt
3 tbsp oil

Clean and cut the root end of the mushroom.
Separate into small bundles.
Mix corn starch, paprika, garlic powder and salt in a bowl.
Toss the mushrooms in the corn starch mixture.
Heat oil in a pan.

This clip features Charlie Houpert explaining a simple shift that changes the psychology of an interview.

Most candidates freeze when they hear:

âDo you have any questions for us?â

They either say noâ¦
or ask something generic.

But this question changes the dynamic:

âIf weâre sitting here one year from now, what would I have done to make you glad you hired me?â

Now the conversation flips.

The interviewer stops evaluating you as a candidate and starts imagining you already succeeding in the role.

Thatâs strategic thinking.

In business and career growth, the people who win are the ones who understand incentives and expectations early.

Clarity creates leverage.

And the people who ask better questions often get better opportunities.
